sources.title: Friend meetup at Bryant Park reviews | Exa place listing
sources.text: I had so much fun walking through Bryant Park on my way to see the NYC Public Library. There was a Lunar New Year celebration taking place. I watched an adorable group of kids perform an ice skating routine, then watched the New York Chinese Cultural Center Lions perform (watch the video I posted, it was awesome). Next trip back to NYC I'll have to see what adventure Bryant Park holds in store for me. Midtown's backyard. Grab a coffee, snag one of those green chairs, and just exist. Ice skating in winter, movies in summer, ping pong tables, chess, random pop-ups. Bathrooms are clean which is a miracle. Gets busy but never feels chaotic. Right behind the library. Solid spot. I just love Bryant Park at Christmas. The winter village is really nice, with lots of options for seasonal food, drinks and activities (including gift shopping, ice skating, and a carousel). The decorations are always tasteful and the fact that the park sits between the majestic National Library building at one end and a lovely French restaurant at the other gives it a very charming feel. Visited in February. Great place to relax. Ice rink is a free admission but with a catch, if you bring your own skates. Otherwise it’s about $20 to rent skates. Great park overall

description.value: Friend meetup at Bryant Park is an easy, free Midtown plan. The park sits between 40th and 42nd Streets and Fifth and Sixth Avenues behind the New York Public Library's Stephen A. Schwarzman building, and its October hours are Daily, 7am-10pm. Tripadvisor's listing (search snapshot) notes that The outdoor Reading Room has picture books and summertime story times, and in winter visitors can Take a spin on the free ice-skating rink. The park also has a landmarked comfort station with staffed public restrooms. Tripadvisor shows 4.6 of 5 bubbles (24,056 reviews) in the same snapshot. Representative Tripadvisor praise (search snapshot): “Fantastic place to visit around the Holidays.” Representative watch-outs: “Maybe the crowds, which are really heavy on the weekends.” and “the food here can be a bit overpriced”.
